text: The Django request/response cycle treats each HTTP request independently: the browser’s URL (e.g., https://example.com/blog/5/) is received, Django matches it to a URL pattern, creates an HttpRequest object, passes it to the view, and the view returns an HttpResponse for that single request [2]. There is no built‑in step that records the request for later use; Django does not keep an open connection or store the request in a session unless you explicitly add that logic [1]. Therefore the server generates the response solely from the current request, not from any previously stored request.
